data.title: Maternal care doesn’t stop at *the clinic door.*
data.lead: Safari ya Mama, “the mother’s journey”, is a companion for the weeks between antenatal visits. It helps mothers recognize warning signs, prepare for care and take the right next step.

data.title: The critical moment may happen *between visits.*
data.lead: Antenatal care provides scheduled moments for assessment and guidance. New symptoms keep their own schedule: at home, at night, far from a clinic. That is when a mother and her family must recognize the sign, decide how urgent it is and reach the right care.

data.symptomText: The next visit is two weeks away. This cannot wait for it.
data.gapText: At a visit, a health worker helps with all three. Between visits, they fall on her and her family. That is the support gap.

data.title: Built on principles, *grounded in reviewed guidance.*
data.lead: MamaBot is a guided companion, not a doctor. These principles decide what it says and what it never does.

principles.title: Empathy first
principles.body: Reproductive health is personal, emotional and often nonlinear.

principles.title: Plain language
principles.body: No one should need a medical degree to understand their own information.

principles.title: Evidence-aware guidance
principles.body: Answers are grounded in reputable medical sources wherever possible.

principles.title: Safety over engagement
principles.body: Urgent symptoms and high-risk situations are escalated clearly.

principles.title: Personalization with restraint
principles.body: Her context improves relevance, without pretending to diagnose.

principles.title: Privacy-conscious design
principles.body: Sensitive reproductive health data deserves careful handling.

principles.title: Support, not replacement
principles.body: It complements professional medical care and never substitutes for it.

data.closingNote: AI explains. Approved rules decide the urgency.
data.ragNote: Urgent messages never reach the model. Every answer is built from the reviewed library and its sources.

ragSteps.title: Safety router first
ragSteps.body: Every message is checked for danger signs. Urgent ones go straight to emergency guidance, with no model involved.

ragSteps.title: Retrieve
ragSteps.body: It finds the matching answer, lesson and sources in the reviewed library, in Kiswahili or English.

ragSteps.title: Augment and generate
ragSteps.body: A language model phrases the retrieved content for her stage and question, without adding new medical claims.

ragSteps.title: Answer with sources
ragSteps.body: She sees the answer, the lesson it came from and when to seek care.

data.rulesText: The warning level comes from a fixed rules engine based on WHO danger signs for pregnancy, the postnatal period and young infants. The same rules (version {rulesVersion}) run on the phone, the server and this website, with shared test cases to prove they agree. The AI can explain a result; it can never change one.
data.liveText: The website talks to MamaBot through a service interface. Setting the API gateway address switches the demo library for the live assistant, while the local safety router keeps running first.

items.title: Mobile-first access
items.body: A small Android app first, with USSD and a paper booklet planned for mothers without a smartphone.

items.title: Offline-first by design
items.body: Checks, lessons and the emergency plan work without data and sync when a connection returns.

items.title: Language localization
items.body: Kiswahili and English today, awaiting native-speaker review. More languages are planned for later regions.

items.title: Local clinical content review
items.body: Rules and lessons are to be signed off by local clinical reviewers against national protocols before enrolment.

items.title: Integration with ANC services
items.body: Consented alerts reach her facility’s dashboard today. Links to national systems through HL7 FHIR and DHIS2 are planned.

items.title: Privacy and consent
items.body: Everything is off until she turns it on. Row-level security, an audit log, and she can download or delete her data.

items.title: Health worker involvement
items.body: Health workers set mothers up, follow up amber and red results and record what they did. Training is part of the pilot plan.

items.title: One shared backend
items.body: The Flutter app, the staff dashboard and this React website use the same secure backend and the same warning rules.

indicators.title: Ability to recognize warning signs
indicators.description: Mothers name danger signs unprompted, at enrolment and at follow-up.

indicators.title: Knowledge of care-seeking actions
indicators.description: Short scenarios: what would you do, and how soon?

indicators.title: Confidence in preparing for care
indicators.description: Self-rated confidence, and whether a birth and emergency plan is complete.

indicators.title: Learning completion and retention
indicators.description: Lessons finished, quiz answers, and a repeat quiz weeks later.

indicators.title: Referral and follow-up completion
indicators.description: Amber and red results followed up within 24 hours; time from red sign to facility contact.

indicators.title: Usability and accessibility
indicators.description: Task-based testing with mothers, including low literacy and shared phones; a standard usability questionnaire.

indicators.title: User engagement
indicators.description: Mothers doing 3 or more checks a week; MamaBot and lesson use.

data.closingText: An independent evaluation is part of the pilot plan. No effect on health outcomes is claimed until it reports.

cards.body: Pilot the app with mothers who attend your ANC clinic.

cards.title: Hospitals and clinics
cards.body: Receive consented alerts, red first, with what she reported.

cards.title: Universities
cards.body: Co-design, usability research and independent evaluation.

cards.title: Researchers
cards.body: Study time from danger sign to care, with ethics approval.

cards.title: Maternal health organizations
cards.body: Content review, protocols and programme design.

cards.title: Community health workers
cards.body: Help mothers set up the app and follow up amber results.

cards.title: Technology partners
cards.body: Connectivity, USSD, hosting and national system links.

footer.note: Safari ya Mama complements antenatal care. It does not replace an assessment by a health worker. In an emergency, go to the nearest health facility.
footer.bottomNote: Demo figures and concept screens are labelled where they appear. No cookies or trackers.
